topicName: Magnetic Effect of an Electric Current
description: This topic explains how an electric current produces a magnetic field, the field patterns around wires, loops and solenoids, the electromagnet and its uses, the motor effect, and the working of a simple direct-current electric motor.

mcq.questionText: Who first discovered that an electric current produces a magnetic field?
mcq.explanation: Oersted noticed that a compass needle was deflected when placed near a wire carrying current, showing that a current produces a magnetic field.

mcq.questionText: When a compass is placed near a wire carrying a current, the compass needle is observed to:
mcq.explanation: The magnetic field produced by the current acts on the compass needle, causing it to deflect from its normal north-south direction.

mcq.questionText: The magnetic field lines around a long straight current-carrying wire are:

options.text: straight lines parallel to the wire

mcq.explanation: Around a straight wire the field forms concentric (circular) loops centred on the wire, lying in planes perpendicular to the wire.

mcq.questionText: Which rule is used to find the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire?
mcq.explanation: In the right-hand grip rule the thumb points in the direction of the current and the curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field.

mcq.questionText: A coil of many turns of insulated wire wound in the form of a long cylinder is called a:
mcq.explanation: A solenoid is a long cylindrical coil of wire; when current flows through it, it behaves like a bar magnet.

mcq.questionText: The magnetic field inside a current-carrying solenoid is:
mcq.explanation: Inside a solenoid the fields of the turns add up to give a strong, nearly uniform field similar to that inside a bar magnet.

options.text: rubbing a steel bar with a permanent magnet
passing current through a coil wound on a soft-iron core

mcq.explanation: An electromagnet is a coil wound on a soft-iron core; it becomes magnetic only while current flows through the coil.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following will NOT increase the strength of an electromagnet?

options.text: Increasing the number of turns of the coil
Increasing the current through the coil
Using a soft-iron core instead of air
Reducing the current in the coil

mcq.explanation: Strength increases with more turns, larger current and a soft-iron core. Reducing the current weakens the electromagnet.

mcq.questionText: A soft-iron core is preferred in an electromagnet because it:

options.text: stays magnetised permanently after the current is switched off
is magnetised easily and loses magnetism quickly when current stops
does not become magnetic at all

mcq.explanation: Soft iron is easily magnetised and demagnetised, so the electromagnet works only while current flows, which is what is needed for devices like bells and relays.

mcq.questionText: Which device uses an electromagnet to switch on a separate, more powerful circuit using a small current?
mcq.explanation: A relay uses a small current in its electromagnet to close (or open) contacts that control a separate, larger circuit.

mcq.questionText: The turning effect (force) on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field is called the:
mcq.explanation: When a current-carrying conductor lies in a magnetic field it experiences a force; this is the motor effect, used in electric motors.

mcq.questionText: Which rule is used to find the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
mcq.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule: thumb = thrust (force/motion), first finger = field, second finger = current.

mcq.questionText: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the first (fore) finger points in the direction of the:
mcq.explanation: The first finger represents the Field, the second finger the Current, and the thumb the Thrust (force).

mcq.questionText: In a simple d.c. motor, the device that reverses the current direction in the coil every half turn is the:
mcq.explanation: The split-ring commutator reverses the current in the coil every half turn so that the coil keeps rotating in the same direction.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy?
mcq.explanation: An electric motor uses the motor effect to turn electrical energy into mechanical energy of rotation.

fib.questionText: The discovery that a current produces a magnetic field was made by the scientist named _____.
fib.explanation: Hans Christian Oersted observed a compass needle deflecting near a current-carrying wire.

fib.questionText: The magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire form _____ circles around the wire.
fib.explanation: The field lines are concentric circles centred on the wire and perpendicular to it.

fib.questionText: The rule in which the thumb points along the current and the fingers curl in the direction of the field is the right-hand _____ rule.
fib.explanation: The right-hand grip rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around a straight wire.

fib.questionText: A long cylindrical coil that behaves like a bar magnet when carrying current is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A solenoid produces a strong, almost uniform field inside it, like a bar magnet.

fib.questionText: The core used in an electromagnet is made of _____ iron because it is easily magnetised and demagnetised.
fib.explanation: Soft iron gains and loses magnetism easily, making it ideal for an electromagnet core.

fib.questionText: The strength of an electromagnet increases when the number of _____ in the coil is increased.
fib.explanation: More turns of wire produce a stronger magnetic field for the same current.

fib.questionText: The force experienced by a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field is known as the _____ effect.
fib.explanation: This force is the basis of how electric motors work.

fib.questionText: The direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is found using Fleming's _____-hand rule.
fib.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule relates field, current and force directions.

fib.questionText: In a simple d.c. motor, the _____ commutator reverses the current in the coil every half turn.
fib.explanation: The split-ring commutator keeps the coil rotating in one direction.

fib.questionText: An electric motor changes electrical energy into _____ energy.
fib.explanation: A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.

tf.questionText: A steady electric current flowing in a wire produces a magnetic field around it.
tf.explanation: This is the magnetic effect of a current, first shown by Oersted.

tf.questionText: The magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire is made of straight lines parallel to the wire.
tf.explanation: The field lines are concentric circles around the wire, not straight parallel lines.

tf.questionText: Reversing the direction of the current reverses the direction of the magnetic field it produces.
tf.explanation: The field direction depends on the current direction, as shown by the right-hand grip rule.

tf.questionText: A current-carrying solenoid has a north pole and a south pole like a bar magnet.
tf.explanation: A solenoid behaves like a bar magnet, with distinct north and south poles at its ends.

tf.questionText: An electromagnet keeps its magnetism permanently even after the current is switched off.
tf.explanation: An electromagnet with a soft-iron core loses almost all its magnetism when the current stops.

tf.questionText: Increasing the current in the coil of an electromagnet increases its strength.
tf.explanation: A larger current produces a stronger magnetic field, so the electromagnet becomes stronger.

tf.questionText: An electric bell uses an electromagnet to make the hammer strike the gong repeatedly.
tf.explanation: In an electric bell the electromagnet attracts an armature that breaks the circuit, so the hammer strikes and resets repeatedly.

tf.questionText: Fleming's right-hand rule is used to find the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
tf.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule is used for the force in a motor; the right-hand rule is used for generators.

tf.questionText: A current-carrying conductor placed parallel to a magnetic field experiences the maximum force.
tf.explanation: The force is maximum when the conductor is at right angles to the field; when parallel, the force is zero.

tf.questionText: A split-ring commutator allows the coil of a d.c. motor to keep turning in the same direction.
tf.explanation: By reversing the current every half turn, the commutator keeps the turning force acting in one rotational direction.

summary.correctAnswer: It showed that an electric current produces a magnetic field, because a compass needle near a current-carrying wire is deflected.
summary.explanation: This was the first evidence linking electricity and magnetism.

summary.questionText: Describe the shape of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire.
summary.correctAnswer: Concentric circles around the wire, lying in planes at right angles to the wire.
summary.explanation: The field is strongest near the wire and weakens with distance.

summary.correctAnswer: If the right hand grips the wire with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current, the curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field.
summary.explanation: It gives the field direction around a straight wire.

summary.questionText: How does a current-carrying solenoid behave magnetically?
summary.correctAnswer: It behaves like a bar magnet, with a north pole at one end and a south pole at the other and a strong, nearly uniform field inside.
summary.explanation: The fields of all the turns add together inside the solenoid.

summary.questionText: List three factors that increase the strength of an electromagnet.
summary.correctAnswer: Increasing the number of turns of the coil, increasing the current, and using a soft-iron core.
summary.explanation: These factors increase the magnetic field produced by the electromagnet.

summary.questionText: Why is soft iron used as the core of an electromagnet?
summary.correctAnswer: Because it is magnetised easily and loses its magnetism quickly when the current is switched off.
summary.explanation: This makes the electromagnet act only while current flows, which suits devices like bells and relays.

summary.correctAnswer: Electric bell, relay, magnetic crane for lifting scrap iron, and loudspeaker (also telephone earpiece).
summary.explanation: Electromagnets are widely used because their magnetism can be switched on and off.

summary.correctAnswer: Hold the thumb, first finger and second finger of the left hand at right angles: first finger points along the field, second finger along the current, and the thumb gives the direction of the force (motion).
summary.explanation: It gives the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

summary.questionText: What is the function of the split-ring commutator in a d.c. motor?
summary.correctAnswer: It reverses the direction of the current in the coil every half turn so the coil keeps rotating in the same direction.
summary.explanation: Without it the coil would oscillate and stop instead of rotating continuously.

summary.questionText: Explain the energy change that takes place in an electric motor.
summary.correctAnswer: It converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.
summary.explanation: The motor effect produces a turning force that rotates the coil.

hoq.questionText: A scrapyard uses a large electromagnet on a crane to lift heavy iron objects. When the operator wants to drop a load of iron at a new place, what should be done?

options.text: Increase the current in the electromagnet
Switch off the current to the electromagnet
Add more turns to the coil
Replace the soft-iron core with steel

hoq.explanation: Because the core is soft iron, switching off the current removes the magnetism almost completely, so the iron load is released.

hoq.questionText: In a simple d.c. motor the coil starts rotating but stops after exactly half a turn and does not continue. Which fault most likely causes this?

options.text: The magnetic field is too strong
The split-ring commutator is faulty and does not reverse the current
The coil has too many turns

hoq.explanation: If the commutator does not reverse the current after a half turn, the turning force reverses and the coil cannot keep rotating in one direction.

hoq.questionText: A straight wire carrying current passes horizontally from west to east between the poles of a magnet, with the magnetic field pointing from north to south (horizontally). Using Fleming's left-hand rule, in which direction does the force on the wire act?
hoq.explanation: By Fleming's left-hand rule, the first finger points north-to-south (field) and the second finger points west-to-east (current); the thumb then points vertically downwards, giving the direction of the force on the wire.
